catalog_quote: Contrastive stress or accent can arise only through morphology. On the phonological level stress is not contrastive. ... A simple pitch-accent system assigns relative high and low pitch to every syllable in a word, with the accent on the syllable that sounds loudest and has the highest pitch. ... The default pattern for two syllable words is accent on the second syllable, with low pitch on the first ... The default pattern for three syllable words is accent and accompanying high pitch on the final syllable ... The default pattern for four syllable words is accent on the final syllable ... Words that consist of more than four syllables are usually verb roots with a string of affixes. In this type of word stress is contrastive on the morphological level and overrules previous pitch patterns. ... there is only one accent per word • default accent is on the final syllable ... sources.quote: Brag-bar (another Northern Situ dialect under situ1238) has a tono-accentual system: lexical words distinguish 'le ton haut (...σ-σ-σ́), le ton tombant (...σ-σ-σ̂), l'accent pénultième (...σ-σ́-σ), et très rare l'accent initial (σ́-σ-σ)'; minimal pairs H vs HL exist but are few (tə-rpí 'graine' vs tə-rpî 'son de blé'); accent is culminative (one per tonal group); accented prefixes in verbal inflection introduce initial accent (2.4.4). sources.locator: ch. 2 Phonologie, section 2.4 'Tons et accents', pp. 79-89 (esp. 2.4.1.2-2.4.1.3 pp. 80-82; 2.4.2.1 p. 82; 2.4.3 pp. 88-89)
sources.note: Only other full grammar-length description under glottocode situ1238 (Glottolog-listed); its 2.4 'Tons et accents' shows Brag-bar Situ has lexical H vs HL tone plus culminative default-final accent and accented verbal prefixes, documenting dialect divergence within the languoid our record is keyed to.

sources.citation: Lin, You-Jing. 2012. By no means marginal: Privative tone in Zhuokeji Rgyalrong. Language and Linguistics 13(4): 625-662.
sources.quote: For the Zhuokeji/Cogtse dialect of Situ (same glottocode): 'Zhuokeji Rgyalrong is a tone language that exhibits a privative system in which /HL/ contrasts with /Ø/. The basic domain of the tonal contrast is the word'; surface patterns of toneless words L-H, L-H-H, L-H-H-L derived by bidirectional foot parsing with H on foot heads and default L; tone alternations mark many grammatical categories (vocative, evidentials, etc.). Earlier accounts (Hsieh 1999, Y. Lin 2000/2003) treated it as accent (every word accented, final accent with Level vs Falling).
sources.locator: abstract p. 625; section 2 pp. 626-628; section 3 tone rules pp. 631-632
sources.note: Dedicated prosody article on the Cogtse/Zhuokeji dialect of the same languoid (the dialect Prins herself contrasts with Kyom-kyo, citing Lin 2009); establishes privative /HL/ vs /Ø/ word tone there. Needed for a dialect-scope caution on the situ1238 record.
